call_sites: reckon/crew_follow_commands.py:3324 the producer path enters runs_module.follower_registration(...) as a context manager, whose finally at reckon/crew/follower_registration.py:510 releases with the reason
reckon/crew_follow_commands.py:3318 the station path's finally calls _StationRegistration.release(), which delegates to _FollowerRegistration.release at reckon/crew_follow_commands.py:184
reckon/crew/follower_registration.py:428 follower_claim wraps follower_registration, so any caller of follower_claim also leaves the record

findings.text: non-blocking: the restore loop calls signal.signal(signum, previous) with no suppression, but signal.signal returns None when the displaced handler was not installed from Python and signal.signal(sig, None) then raises TypeError; that raise lands inside the context manager's finally and skips registration.release(reason) at :510, so the exit record this node exists to write is lost. The sibling helper serve.py:4249-4255 suppresses (ValueError, TypeError) for exactly this case.

non-blocking: the exit-record write runs before the flock release and is not guarded, so a write failure (a read-only or full crew home) propagates out of release(); release() is called from a finally on both delivery branches, so that failure replaces the follower's original exit and reports a settle to the session host as a crash.

non-blocking: the landed fragment states the base importer population as '142 passed and 2 failed, both reexec probes in a non-git tree'; the manifest's evidence_inputs.base_arm_correction records that cause as superseded (the failures were the node's own git-archive extraction racing the run) and logs/baseline-population.log shows 144 passed EXIT=0 on an undisturbed base tree. The conclusion (adds no failure) stands, but the fragment carries a cause the node has already retracted.

non-blocking: the SIGTERM install/restore here duplicates the capability already owned by _install_termination_unwind/_remove_termination_unwind in reckon/serve.py:4234-4255 rather than extending it; parameterising the exception the handler raises would leave one implementation, and the copy has already lost the owner's TypeError suppression (see the finding at :508).

non-blocking: every case drives the registration context manager from a synthetic driver rather than the crew follow command, so a regression in the production follower's own exit path (crew_follow_commands.py:3299 and :3318) would not redden this file; the four cases guard the registration's release, not the command that reaches it.
